name: Aldous
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Mo Ji' was fully localized to the US-style name 'Aldous', consistent with the renaming of his Flame Demon Holy Land companions (Mo Xiao becoming 'Lamar', Mo Wuliang/'Infinite Mo' becoming 'Reuben').
description: A Soul Sea Realm master of the Flaming Place who appears in Episodes 945-947 alongside Lamar and Reuben. When their begging fails, the three flee in separate directions; the young man in black cuts down Reuben first and then shoots toward Aldous, killing the trio one by one. The scene matches the source chapter 924 slaughter of Mo Xiao, Mo Wuliang, and Mo Ji.

name: War Lords War Generals and War Fighters
localized_canonical: War Lords War Generals and War Fighters
reason: Extraction artifact: the Ep 946 sentence 'countless War Lords, War Generals, and War Fighters were locked in a bloody struggle' is a list of three generic military rank terms, not a single entity.
description: Not an entity; a concatenated list of the generic warrior ranks War Lord, War General, and War Fighter.

name: Aliza
reason: The source epithet 'Evil Moon' was replaced with the personal name 'Aliza' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A legendary figure invoked in Episode 950: the last warrior to earn the Golden Celestial Paragon rank, four hundred thousand years ago, before becoming a Supreme Lord. Only six warriors in known history ever earned that rank. Matches the source's 'Evil Moon', the last Gold Demi-Immortal title holder who became a Celestial Master 400,000 years prior; the character never appears on-page and no gender is evidenced.

name: Silver Berserker Rank
reason: The source talent title 'Silver Asura' was renamed 'Silver Berserker Rank' to avoid the Buddhist-Hindu loanword and fit the Western fantasy register.
description: A rare silver-tier talent title earned on the Talent Tablet, higher than Max's own title but still a gulf below a Gold title such as the Golden Celestial Paragon. Kade earns it in Episodes 951-953, surpassing seven Demi-Immortal Race prodigies at once, and Yolande vows to protect him for it. Corresponds to the source's 'Silver Asura' title earned by Zhao Li in the Tower of Sin arc.

name: Violet-Core Physique Cora
reason: Extraction artifact: a span bridging two entities in sentences like 'After awakening her First-Rank Violet-Core Physique, Cora had...'. The physique and the character Cora are separate, already-tracked entities.
description: Not an entity; a false merge of 'Violet-Core Physique' and the character 'Cora'.

name: Third-Rank Blue-Violet Core
reason: The source grade 'third-grade Deep Purple' of the Extreme Purple Yin Body was localized as 'Third-Rank Blue-Violet Core' to match the show's 'Violet-Core Physique' terminology.
description: A high grade of the Violet-Core Physique, ranked just below the Second-Rank Pure-Violet Core. In Episodes 965-966, the sheer number of giant swords Cora pulls down convinces observers that someone with at least a Third-Rank Blue-Violet Core must be responsible, drawing the Violet Ascendancy Sect's leader to investigate.

name: Leah Jones
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhao Xiaoxiao' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Leah Jones', a sultry, approachable name fitting her seductress archetype as leader of the Siren's Kiss Sect (source 'Ecstasy House').
description: The sultry, barely-dressed leader of the Siren's Kiss Sect, one of the three great sects of the Violet Core Realm famous across the universe and a bitter rival of Krista Donovan's Violet Ascendancy Sect. In Episode 967 she tries to recruit Cora, offering the company of any man she desires and the sect's Coupled Cultivation methods. Matches the source's Zhao Xiaoxiao of the Ecstasy House.

name: Cloudy Mountains
issues: Possible name drift: early episodes (~Ep 134-146) place Dragon Valley and the keep's map location in the 'Misty Peaks', while Eps 974/995 use 'Cloudy Mountains'; 'Misty Peak' is also used for the Skyreach Sect's mountain, so the later rename may have been made to avoid a collision.
reason: The source location 'Nine Yin Mountain' was renamed 'Cloudy Mountains' to drop the yin-yang reference and fit the Western fantasy register.
description: The mountain range containing Dragon Valley, the site of The Elysian Keep that Zane once entered. In Episode 974 the 'secret place' he is led to turns out to be Dragon Valley in the Cloudy Mountains, and in Episode 995 a burst of insight conjures a miniature replica of the keep there. Corresponds to the source's Nine Yin Mountain and its Jade Dragon Valley, entrance to the Immortal Mansion.

name: Great Theurgy
reason: The source's generic description of the Immortal Mansion owner's 'great divine abilities' that let him 'predict everything in the world' was given the proper name 'Great Theurgy' in the adaptation.
description: The all-perceiving divinatory power attributed to the Master who owns The Elysian Keep, a being who transcended the universe. In Episode 988 the Eternal Scribe reasons that the Master foresaw Zane entering The Archives and arranged events for him, though Zane, a man without a Destiny whose future no one can read, suspects it may be coincidence.

name: Primordial Chaos
reason: The source term 'Primal Chaos' (and its 'Secret Technique of Primal Chaos') was rendered 'Primordial Chaos' for the Western fantasy register; the episodes also use the fuller form 'Primordial Chaos Tactic' for the cultivation method.
description: The Chaos energy existing outside the world, and the perilous cultivation path built on it. Zane's Master theorized the Primordial Chaos Tactic but never dared walk the path himself; Zane practices it, filling his Inner World with Chaos Energy instead of Vitality, and spends three agonizing months lost in its pain (Eps 994-995) while the world itself begins rejecting what it cannot categorize.
